name: Tulil
confidence_why: The only modern grammar, Meng 2018, hears prominence mostly on the last syllable but calls her own stress analysis very preliminary, auditory-only and non-contrastive and doubts that Tulil has prominent word-level stress at all, so the record is left undetermined on that single first-hand source with nothing contradicting it.
catalog_citation: Meng, Chenxi. 2018. A grammar of Tulil. PhD thesis, La Trobe University. doi:10.26181/21857724 (open PDF via La Trobe figshare/OPAL).
catalog_locator: sec. 2.4.1 'Stress', printed p. 27 (p. 58); supporting hedge in sec. 2.2 (diphthongs), printed pp. 26-27
catalog_quote: Stress is not contrastively utilized in Tulil words. Note that the stress analysis given here is very preliminary and only based on auditory impression thus far, and Tulil may not be a language that takes word-level stress as a prominent feature as languages like English (cf. Goedemans & van Zanten, 2014). Most Tulil words have their stress on the last syllables, signalled by a combination of slightly higher intensity, lengthening of the vowel and (possibly) vowel quality. Pitch is not a predictable indicator of stress: words in isolation commonly have a higher pitch in the first syllable, while in a sentence the last syllable of a word can get a higher pitch. However, the difference between stressed and unstressed syllables in regard to all these variables is not very prominent, and is subject to the position in an intonation contour. tone.quote: Stress is not contrastively utilized in Tulil words. … Most Tulil words have their stress on the last syllables, signalled by a combination of slightly higher intensity, lengthening of the vowel and (possibly) vowel quality. Pitch is not a predictable indicator of stress: words in isolation commonly have a higher pitch in the first syllable, while in a sentence the last syllable of a word can get a higher pitch. However, the difference between stressed and unstressed syllables in regard to all these variables is not very prominent, and is subject to the position in an intonation contour.
tone.summary: Suprasegmentals are only non-contrastive root-final stress and sentence intonation (pitch tracks); word pitch varies with position in the intonation contour; tone never mentioned; 15 C, 6 V.
